subject: Behavioral Economics
title: Buying Time
description: Learn Buying Time in one minute.

hook.text: Hiring someone to clean your house for $80 buys you three hours. People who buy time report greater life satisfaction.

buildup.text: Whillans' research found that using money to eliminate unpleasant tasks increases happiness more than buying luxury.

discovery.text: Time poverty — feeling like you never have enough time — is a stronger predictor of unhappiness than income poverty.

twist.text: But people methodically choose material purchases over time-saving ones, even when they can afford both.

climax.text: Before your next purchase, ask: would I be happier spending this money to buy back my time instead?

punchline.text: The best thing money can buy is time.

quiz.question: What did research find about buying time?
options: It has no effect on happiness
Using money to eliminate unpleasant tasks increases happiness
Only wealthy people benefit from buying time

details.summary: Using money to save time, such as hiring help for cleaning, commuting less, or paying for convenience, produces significant happiness gains. People who prioritize time over money report higher life satisfaction across income levels.
details.whyItMatters: Most people undervalue their time and overspend on material goods. Research suggests outsourcing disliked tasks is one of the most effective uses of discretionary income for improving daily wellbeing and reducing stress.
takeaways: Spending money to save time reliably increases happiness
People who value time over money report greater life satisfaction
Even small time-saving purchases like meal delivery improve daily mood

faq.question: Why do so few people spend money to buy time?
faq.answer: People feel guilty about outsourcing tasks they could do themselves, viewing it as laziness. They also underestimate how much disliked chores drain their energy and mood. The benefits of free time are abstract while the cost is concrete.

faq.question: Does buying time work for people at all income levels?
faq.answer: Yes, the happiness boost from time-saving purchases appears across income brackets. Even modest investments like paying for grocery delivery or a laundry service produce measurable improvements in daily mood and stress levels.
